Genetics                       Event  Category:  Health  Professions
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor  Round  Two:  Skill(s)  assessment   
New  for  2026-2027  This  is  a  new  event  for  2026-2027.    
Event  Summary
 Genetics  provides  HOSA  Members  the  opportunity  to  gain  the  knowledge  and  skills  required  for  a  laboratory  setting  and  to  
explore
 
genetics-related
 
careers.
 
This
 
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds.
 
Round
 
One
 
is
 
a
 
written,
 
multiple-choice
 
test,
 
and
 
the
 
top-scoring
 
competitors
 
will
 
advance
 
to
 
Round
 
Two
 
for
 
the
 
skills
 
assessment.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
learn
 
more
 
about
 
the
 
careers
 
available.
  
Sponsorship
 
HOSA-  Future  Health  Professionals  appreciates  the  sponsorship  of  this  event  by  Carolina  Biological  Supply  Company.   Carolina  Biological  Supply  Company  has  developed  a  special  landing  page for  HOSA  competitors  and  advisors.  
 
 
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   ●  Round  One:  Proper  business  attire,  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform,  or  attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.    ●  Round  Two:  Attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.  
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID for  both  rounds  ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  eraser  for  the  test.  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  ●  Safety  glasses  or  goggles  ●  Disposable  gown  (PPE)  ●  Disposable  non-latex  gloves   ●  Full-face  shield  (or  equivalent  PPE)  ●  Disposable  masks  with  ties  or  loops  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.

ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. 
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Written  Test  Plan  The  written  test  for  Genetics  is:  ●  Reproduction,  Mitosis  and  Meiosis-  20%  ●  Classical  Genetics-  20%  ●  Chromosomal  Inheritance-  10%   
 Genetics  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  2  of  13  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

●  Experimental  Design  and  Model  Organisms-   15%  ●  Molecular  Genetics-  15  %  ●  Population  Genetics-  10%  ●  Modern  Applications  and  Careers  in  Genetics-  10%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  During  which  phase  of  the  cell  cycle  is  DNA  replicated?  (Teaching  the  Cell  Cycle  and  Mitosis  -  Carolina  Knowledge  Center) A.  G1  B.  S  C.  G2  D.  M  2.  A  cross  between  white  eyed  female  drosophila  and  red  eyed  male  drosophila  produced  the  F1  generation  below  F1  Red  Eyes  White  Eyes  Female  6  0  Male  0  6  From  the  F1  generation,  crossing  a  red-eyed  female  with  a  white  eyed  male  produced   F2  Red  Eyes  White  Eyes  Female  5  5  Male  5  5  Using  the  charts  above  which  of  the  following  inheritance  patterns  matches  the  data  of  this  cross  for  white  eye  color?   (Genetics  with  Drosophila  F1  Crosses:  Sex-Linkage  |  Carolina  Biological  Supply)  A.  Simple  dominance   B.  Codominance   C.  Incomplete  dominance  D.  X-linked  trait  
 3.  What  type  of  mutation  has  occurred  to  the  DNA  strand  shown  above?  (Modeling-DNA-to-Protein_NSTA-DENVER-2024.pdf)  A.  Frameshift  –  addition  B.  Frameshift  –  deletion  C.  Translocation  D.  Substitution    
ROUND  TWO-  Skills  Assessment
 
1.  The  top  competitors  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  competitors  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  Round  Two  is  a  selected  skill(s)  performance.  The  Round  Two  skills  approved  for  this  event  are:  Skill  I:  DNA  Extraction  20  minutes  
Skill  II-A:  Perform  Gene  Transfer  with  Asexually  Reproducing  Organism  (E.Coli)  Bacterial  Conjugation  
20  minutes  
 Genetics  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  3  of  13  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

Skill  II-B:  Perform  Gene  Transfer  with  Asexually  Reproducing  Organism  (E.Coli)  Bacterial  Transduction  
20  minutes  
Skill  III-A:  Perform  Test  Genetic  Cross  with  Sexually  Reproducing  Model  Organism  
25  minutes  
Skill  III-B:   Perform  Test  Genetic  Cross  with  Sexually  Reproducing  Model  Organism-  Wisconsin  Fast  Plants  
 
25  minutes  
Skill  IV:  Genetic  Cross  Results  Interpretation  15  minutes  
Skill  V:  Validate  Mode  of  Inheritance  Using  Chi-Square  Test  15  minutes  3.  For  all  skills,  body  ﬂuids  will  be  simulated  products.              
4.  The  selected  skill(s)  will  be  presented  to  competitors  as  a  written  scenario  at  the  beginning  of  the  round.  The  scenario  will  be  the  same  for  each  competitor.  A  sample  scenario  can  be  found here. Some  scenarios  may  involve  the  combination  of  multiple  skills.  If  the  event  rating  sheets  are  combined,  it  is  not  necessary  to  repeat  a  task  a  second  time.   An  example  would  be  competitors  would  not  need  to  identify  the  patient  twice.  
5.  Timing  will  begin  when  the  scenario  is  presented  to  the  competitors  and  will  be  stopped  at  the  end  of  the  time  allowed.  The  scenario  is  a  secret  topic.  Competitors  MAY  NOT  discuss  or  reveal  the  secret  topic  until  after  the  event  has  concluded  or  will  face  penalties  per  the  GRRs.   
6.  Competitors  must  complete  all  skill  steps  listed  in  the  guidelines,  even  if  the  steps  must  be  simulated/verbalized.  (If  the  equipment  is  available,  the  competitors  would  complete  all  skill  steps  as  the  scenario  warrants.  The  competitors  will  simulate/verbalize  the  steps  if  the  equipment  is  unavailable.)  
7.  Judges  will  provide  information  to  competitors  as  directed  by  the  rating  sheets.  Competitors  may                ask  questions  of  the  judges  while  performing  skills,  if  the  questions  relate  to  patient’s  condition  and                will  be  included  in  the  scenario  or  judge  script.  
8.  Competitors  must  use  all  equipment  correctly  and  safely.  Judges  will  stop  a  student  and  not  award  points  for  a  step  if  they  see  a  competitor  is  about  to  cause  a  risk  of  harm  or  about  to  damage  equipment  or  other  supplies.   
Final  Scoring 
 1.  The  competitor  must  earn  a  score  of  70%  or  higher  on  the  combined  skill(s)  of  the  event  in  order  to  be  recognized  as  
an
 
award
 
winner
 
at
 
the
 
ILC.
 
  2.  The  ﬁnal  rank  is  determined  by  adding  the  round  one  test  score  plus  the  round  two  skill  score.  In  the  event  of  a  tie,  
the
 
highest
 
test
 
score
 
will
 
be
 
used
 
to
 
determine
 
the
 
ﬁnal
 
placement.
  
Future  Opportunities  The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.

to

and

opportunity
 
to

Genetics   Skill  I:  DNA  Extraction
 
Time:  20  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  _______ SS  ________ PS/C     Judge’s  Signature: _________________________
 
 Skill  I:    DNA  Extraction  Possible  Awarded  
1.   
Entered  testing  area  wearing  closed-toed  shoes,  then  donned  proper  PPE:  glasses/safety  glasses/goggles  and  gloves  (lab  coat  is  optional).  
2  0    
2.   
Obtained  DNA  source,  placed  in  bag,  sealed  bag,  and  gently  mashed  with  hands  for  2  minutes.  
2  0    
3.   
Measured  10  ml  of  extraction  buffer,  poured  into  bag,  and  mashed  with  hands  for  one  additional  minute  
    2      0    
4.   
Placed  funnel  into  50  ml  centrifuge  tube,  folded  cheesecloth  and  placed  it  into  the  funnel  to  create  a  ﬁlter.           
2  0    
5.  
Poured  mixture  into  the  ﬁlter,  ﬁltering  the  contents  through  the  cheesecloth  into  the  50-ml  centrifuge  tube  
2  0    
6.  
Carefully  poured  2  ml  of  the  ﬁltered  contents  from  the  50  –  ml  tube  into  a  clean  15  –  ml  tube.   
1  0    
7.  
Used  a  transfer  pipette  to  measure  and  add  5  ml  of  chilled  95%  ethanol  to  the  15-ml  tube   
2  0    
8.  
Inserted  and  rotated  wooden  stick  or  transfer  pipette  in  ethanol  directly  above  the  extract  layer  to  wind  (or  “spool”)  DNA  
2  0    
9.  
Transferred  DNA  from  wooden  stick  or  transfer  pipette  into  1.5  ml  tube.   
2  0    
10.  
Cleaned  up  work  area  by  disposing  of  bags,  cheesecloth,  and  used  50  and  15  ml  tubes  
1  0    
11.  
Cleaned  work  surface  with  disinfectant  
1  0    
12.  
Removed  PPE  
1  0    
Total  Points-  Skill  I:   70%  Mastery  for  Skill  I:  14   
20

Genetics  Skill  II-A:  Perform  Gene  Transfer  with  Asexually  Reproducing  Model  Organism  (E.  Coli)  Bacterial  Conjugation  Time:  20  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  _______ SS  ________ PS/C      Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
Skill  II-A:  Perform  Gene  Transfer  with  Asexually  Reproducing  Model  Organism  (E.  Coli)-  Bacterial  Conjugation   
Possible  Awarded  
    
1.
  
Entered  testing  area  wearing  closed-toed  shoes,  then  donned  proper  PPE:  glasses/safety  glasses/goggles  and  gloves  (lab  coat  is  optional).  
2  0    Observe  Conﬁrmation  Plates  
2.
  
Examined  the  prepared  conﬁrmation  plates  and  recorded  the  observed  results.  
    2      0    Prepare  “Mating”  Plate  
3.  
Used  correct  sterile  technique  to  dip  a  sterile  inoculating  loop  into  the  liquid  culture  of  Strain  1   
2  0    
4.  Placed  a  drop  of  culture  on  the  LB  mating  plate  by  touching  the  inoculated  loop  to  the  agar.  
2  0    
5.  
Used  a  new  loop  and  the  liquid  culture  of  strain  II  to  place  a  drop  of  strain  II  1/2inch  from  the  drop  of  the  strain  1  on  the  mating  plate   
2  0    
6.  Used  a  new  sterile  loop  to  mix  strains  1  and  II  over  surface  of  mating  plate.    
2  0    
7.  Allowed  the  liquid  on  the  plate  to  soak  in  completely  and  inverts  plate.   
1  0    
8.  
Vocalizes  “Incubate  plates  for  24-48  hours  at  room  temperature  (37C)”  
1  0    Testing  for  Recombination:  Transferred  some  bacterial  cells  from  the  mating  plate  to  LB+amp,  LB+str,  and  LB+str+amp  plates  using  correct  sterile  technique.  Judges:  one  point  awarded  per  step  per  plate  (3  plates  total)  for  steps  9-12  below  9.  
Used  correct  sterile  technique  to  remove  a  sterile  inoculating  loop  from  the  package  by  opening  it  from  the  handle  end  
3  0    
10.  Slightly  lifted  the  lid  of  the  mating  plate  and  picked  up  bacteria.  Closed  lid.  
3  0    
11.  
Streaked  some  bacteria  onto  plate  (to  LB+amp,  LB+str,  and  LB+str+amp).  Plate  was  opened  as  little  as  possible  during  this  step  
3  0    
12.  Discarded  the  loop  in  the  disposal  container  or  replace  it  into  its  wrapper  for  disposal  later.  
3  0    
13.  Taped  plates  together  
1  0    
14.  
Vocalizes  “Incubate  plates  for  24-48  hours  at  room  temperature  (37C)”  
1  0    
15.  
Cleaned  up  work  area  and  cleaned  work  surface  with  disinfectant  
1  0    
16.  
Removed  PPE.  
1  0    
Total  Points-  Skill  II-A:   70%  Mastery  for  Skill  II-A:  21   
30

Genetics  Skill  II-B:  Perform  Gene  Transfer  with  Asexually  Reproducing  Model  Organism  (E.  Coli)  Bacterial  Transduction  
Time:
 
20
 
minutes
 Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  _______ SS  ________ PS/C     Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
Skill  II-B:  Perform  Gene  Transfer  with  Asexually  Reproducing  Model  Organism  (E.  Coli)-  
Bacterial
 
Transduction
 
(Essential
 
Lab
 
Skill
 
Performed-
 
Serial
 Dilution)  
Possible  Awarded  
1.   Entered  testing  area  wearing  closed-toed  shoes,  then  donned  proper  PPE:  glasses/safety  glasses/goggles  and  gloves  (lab  coat  is  optional).  
2  0    
2.   Labeled  four  sterile  culture  tubes  “BE.”  Label  four  other  sterile  culture  tubes  “CR63.”  
1  0    
3.   On  one  of  the  BE  tubes  and  one  of  the  CR63  tubes,  wrote  “undiluted”  (or  “UD”  for  short).  On  a  second  BE  tube  and  a  second  CR63  tube,  wrote  “1:10.”  On  a  third  BE  tube  and  a  third  CR63  tube,  wrote  “1:100.”  On  the  remaining  tube  of  each  set,  wrote  “no  phage.”  
    1      0    
4.  Used  a  sterile  transfer  pipet  to  place  0.5  mL  of  E.  coli  BE  culture  into  the  four  tubes  labeled  “BE.”  
2  0    
5.   Used  a  sterile  transfer  pipet  to  place  0.5  mL  of  E.  coli  CR63  culture  into  the  four  tubes  labeled  CR63.  
2  0    
              Infect  the  BE  and  CR63  cultures  with  undiluted  bacteriophage                *  Judge:  one  point  awarded  per  step  per  culture  tube  (2  total)  for  steps  6-8  below
 
6.  Added  10  μ L  of  undiluted  transducing  lysate  to  the  tube  of  BE  cells  &  CR63  labeled  “undiluted.” *  *Assessment  does  not  include  use  of  micropipettes.  Fixed  volume  or  other  methods  of  liquid  transfer  are  permitted.  
2  0    
7.  Disposed  of  the  tip  or  disposable  pipette  used  to  transfer  10  ul  in  the  biological  waste  container.  
2  0    
8.  Gently  ﬂicked  the  bottom  of  the  BE  cells  &  CR63  tubes  to  mix  the  phages  and  cells.  
2  0                  Infect  the  BE  and  CR63  cultures  with  transducing  lysate  that  has  been  diluted  1:10                *Judge:  one  point  awarded  per  step  per  culture  tube  (2  total)  for  steps  9-11  below
 
9.  Added  10  μ L  of  the  1:10  dilution  of  the  transducing  lysate  to  the  tube  of  BE  cells  &  CR63  labeled  “1:10.” *  *Assessment  does  not  include  use  of  micropipettes.  Fixed  volume  or  other  methods  of  liquid  transfer  are  permitted.  
2  0    
10.  Disposed  of  the  tip  or  disposable  pipette  used  to  transfer  10  ul  in  the  biological  waste  container    
2  0    
11.  Gently  ﬂicked  the  bottom  of  the  BE  cells  &  CR63  tubes  to  mix  the  phages  and  cells.  
2  0     Infect  the  BE  and  CR63  cultures  with  transduction  lysate  that  has  been  diluted  1:100                *Judges:  one  point  awarded  per  step  per  culture  tube  (2  total)  for  steps  12-14  below    
 Genetics  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  7  of  13  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

Skill  II-B:  Continued…
 
Possible  Awarded  
12.  Added  10  µ L  of  the  1:100  dilution  of  the  transducing  lysate  to  the  tube  of  BE  cells  &  CR63  labeled  “1:100.” *  *Assessment  does  not  include  use  of  micropipettes.  Fixed  volume  or  other  methods  of  liquid  transfer  are  permitted.  
2  0    
13.  Disposed  of  the  tip  used  or  disposable  pipette  to  transfer  10  ul  in  the  biological  waste  container.  
2  0    
14.  Gently  ﬂicked  the  bottom  of  the  BE  cells  &  CR63  tubes  to  mix  the  phages  and  cells.  
2  0    
15.  Vocalized  “let  all  the  tubes  stand  at  room  temperature  for  5  to  15  minutes.”  
1  0    Plate  the  Phage-Bacteria  Mixtures  
16.  On  the  bottom  of  each  LB/amp  plate,  wrote  “BE,”  the  date,  and  something  to  identify  the  plates  as  belonging  to  the  student.  Wrote  on  the  bottom  of  one  of  these  labeled  LB/amp  plates,  “no  phage,”  on  another,  “undiluted,”  on  a  third,  “1:10,”  and  on  the  fourth,  “1:100.”  
1  0   
 
17.  On  the  bottom  of  each  LB  plate,  wrote  “CR63,”  the  date,  and  something  to  identify  the  plates  as  belonging  to  the  student.  Wrote  on  the  bottom  of  one  of  these  labeled  LB  plates,  “no  phage,”  on  another,  “undiluted,”  on  a  third,  “1:10,”  and  on  the  fourth,  “1:100.”  
2  0   
 
18.  Collected  glass  beads  for  spreading  the  plate.  Turned  the  plates  over  and,  one  at  time,  slightly  open  each  plate  and  shake  four  or  ﬁve  glass  beads  onto  the  lid.  
1  0   
 
19.  Used  sterile  technique,  pour  the  phage  and  bacteria  mixture  from  each  tube  onto  the  correspondingly  labeled  plate.  Lifted  the  lid  of  the  plate  only  long  enough  to  pour  the  contents  of  the  tube  onto  the  plate.  
4  0    
20.  Used  a  back-and-forth  motion  (not  swirling  round  and  round)  to  move  the  glass  beads  across  the  entire  surface  of  each  plate.  
2  0    
21.  Removed  the  glass  beads  from  each  plate  by  holding  the  plate  vertically  over  a  container  designated  for  the  purpose.  Open  the  plate  slightly  (like  a  clamshell)  and  tap  the  beads  into  the  container.  
2  0    
22.  Vocalized”  Incubate  at  37°C  for  1–2  days”   
1  0    
23.  Cleaned  up  work  area  and  cleaned  work  surface  with  disinfectant  
2  0    
24.  Removed  PPE.  
1  0

    Drosophila  Anesthetizing  and  Sexing  
1.   Entered  testing  area  wearing  closed-toed  shoes,  then  donned  proper  PPE:  glasses/safety  glasses/goggles  and  gloves  (lab  coat  is  optional).  
2  0

2  0    
11.  Used  the  measuring  cup  provided  to  add  one  level  measure  of  water  to  each  vial.  
2  0

2  0

2  0

1  0

1  0
